subject: storytime
title: The Lion and the Mouse
about: Aesop's fable of the mighty lion who lets a tiny mouse go and is later set free by her when he is caught in a trap. Fables are the first read-aloud domain of the NC/CKLA Grade 1 year (Fables and Stories), where children learn that a fable is a short story with a lesson, and this is one of the gentlest. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, three pages long.
tip: After the last page, ask: who turned out to be the stronger friend, and how?

book.author: Aesop (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: A tiny mouse pays back a big favor.

passage.text:
A big lion slept in the sun.
A little mouse ran up his back.
The lion woke up.
He grabbed the mouse with his big paw.
"Please let me go," said the mouse.
"One day I will help you."
The lion laughed.
"You are too little to help me!"
But he let the mouse go.
***
One day, some men came to the woods.
They set a trap.
It was a big net.
The lion ran into the net.
He could not get out.
He roared and roared.
"Help! Help!"
The little mouse heard him.
She ran as fast as she could.
***
"I will help you," said the mouse.
She nibbled the net with her sharp teeth.
Nibble, nibble, nibble.
Snap!
The net fell apart.
The lion was free!
"Thank you, little friend," said the lion.
"You were right."
"You did help me."
Little friends can be big friends.

cards.q: Who ran up the lion's back?
cards.note: The mouse is tiny next to the lion, which is the whole point of the story.

cards.q: Where was the lion sleeping at the start?
cards.note: Ask him to find the line on the first page that tells you.

cards.q: What did the men set in the woods?
cards.note: The trap was a big net, and the lion ran right into it.

cards.q: How did the lion call for help?
cards.note: Have him roar like the lion, then squeak like the mouse.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: Retelling in order is a Grade 1 skill: first, next, last.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: The mouse chewed through the net and the lion was free.

cards.q: How did the lion feel when he was stuck in the net?
cards.note: The story never says the word, so he has to work it out from all the roaring.
A fable is a short story with a lesson at the end; this one is the last line.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'nibbled' mean?
cards.note: Mice nibble with small, quick bites; show him with a cracker.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
